newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico central bank rejects pump-priming charge.
newsitem.headline: Mexico central bank rejects pump-priming charge.

text.p: Mexico's central bank said on Wednesday it rejected accusations that it was pump-priming the country's economy in the run-up to July elections.
"We reject that accusation definitely," a Banco de Mexico spokesman told Reuters. He also said a stronger than expected increase in Mexico's monetary base was determined by demand.

"The phenomenon we are witnessing -- the difference between projections and the actual figure -- is demand-determined. The demand is exogenous to the actions of the central bank," the spokesman added.

He said economic strength had fuelled a demand for cash that emerged stronger than the central bank had forecast at the start of the year. "Economic activity and unemployment have come in stronger than expected, and at the same time inflation has come down faster than expected, and this has produced a stronger demand for means of payment," he said.
